items.passage: "Father, the postmaster says the river road is shorter," I told him, spreading the map across the counter. Taeyang did not look at it. __He had folded the corner of every map he owned toward the north, a habit I took for the neatness of a clerk.__ Outside, a cart of melons rolled past the little post office, and the clerk inside weighed our parcel twice, frowning at the scale as though it had insulted him. I paid the fee from my own purse, counting the coins in English under my breath, which made the clerk smile. We had come to send a parcel to my aunt, though Father had written nothing on the label but a name. When the clerk asked where it should go, Father answered with the name of a village I had never once heard him say aloud. He took the map from me, opened its folded corner, and pressed his thumbnail against a small dot beside a river that does not run anywhere near Shanghai. Then he handed the map back to me and asked whether the river road was paved.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It establishes the father's clerical habits as background for the errand at the post office.
It introduces a tidy habit that the clerk's careful weighing of the parcel then echoes.
It shows the general care with which the father treats the objects that he owns.
It hints at a longing for a distant place that the father's later gestures reveal.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 처음에는 아버지의 깔끔한 습관을 보여 주는 배경 묘사처럼 읽힌다. 그러나 뒤에서 아버지는 한 번도 입에 올리지 않던 마을 이름을 말하고, 접어 두었던 지도 모서리를 펼쳐 상하이와 무관한 강가의 점을 짚는다. 이 두 장면이 겹치면서 북쪽으로 접힌 모서리는 고향을 향한 그리움의 복선으로 다시 읽히므로 D가 정답이다. A는 밑줄 문장만 읽은 해석이고, B는 바로 뒤 우체국 장면과 연결한 오독이며, C는 습관을 일반적 성격으로 넓혀 후반 단서를 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: Three rules governed the chess club on the promenade, and Radek had written them himself on a card above the door: no talking during play, no coffee near the boards, no lessons for another member's pupils. __Vesna kept her own clock in a velvet bag, though the club had owned electric ones for twenty years.__ That afternoon the wind off the water rattled the windows, and two old men argued about whether the gulls were louder this year. Radek's pupil, a boy of eleven, sat across from him practicing the sealed move, the old custom of writing a move in an envelope when a game is paused overnight. Hardly anyone under sixty in the club still knew how to do it properly. The boy kept forgetting to stop the clock before he wrote. At six, Vesna rose, crossed to Radek's table, and set the velvet bag beside the envelope. She left without a word. Inside was her clock, its two buttons worn pale, with a slip of paper wedged under the stop lever.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces an object whose later use shows Vesna helping with her rival's lesson.
It portrays Vesna as a member who prefers older equipment to the club's newer clocks.
It sets up a contrast with the noisy argument that the wind and gulls provoke.
It reflects the general resistance to change among the older members of the club.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장만 보면 Vesna가 옛 장비를 고집한다는 성격 묘사처럼 보인다. 그러나 지문 앞부분에는 다른 회원의 제자를 가르치지 말라는 규칙이 있고, 뒷부분에서 소년은 봉인 수를 쓸 때 시계 멈추는 법을 계속 잊는다. Vesna가 그 벨벳 주머니 속 시계를 Radek의 탁자에 두고 가는 장면이 나오면서 밑줄 문장은 경쟁자의 수업을 돕는 행동을 준비하는 장치로 바뀌므로 A가 정답이다. B는 표면 기능만 읽은 것이고, C는 바로 뒤 문장과의 관계로 본 오독이며, D는 지문 표현을 일반화해 결말 행동을 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: Buckets of silt came up the cellar steps all morning, and by noon my brother and I had saved a tin box of our mother's letters. __Talon, who had studied her language for two years in Flagstaff, offered to read them aloud while I laid the pages on the porch to dry.__ Wind moved across the plateau, and a neighbor's dog kept stealing the clothespins I had set out for the wet blankets. I chased it twice and gave up. Talon read slowly, sometimes stopping to rub a smeared word with his thumb. In one letter, he said, she called our father a patient man. Near dusk I found a second copy of that letter folded inside an envelope, written in her careful English for a cousin who could not read Diné. Where Talon had said patient, she had written stubborn as a fence post. I read it twice. When Talon came out with coffee, I handed him the envelope, and he set his cup down on the step without drinking. "Chayton," he said, and then said nothing else.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Talon, rather than the narrator, reads the letters during the cleanup.
It presents Talon as a reliable reader, a role the second letter calls into doubt.
It contrasts Talon's careful reading with the antics of the neighbor's dog outside.
It shows how the flood brings the siblings closer to their mother's language and past.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 단독으로는 왜 Talon이 편지를 읽는지 알려 주는 배경 설명처럼 보인다. 하지만 중간에 Talon은 어머니가 아버지를 '참을성 있는 사람'이라 했다고 전하고, 해 질 무렵 화자는 같은 편지의 영어 사본에서 전혀 다른 표현을 발견한다. 이후 Talon이 커피를 내려놓고 말을 잇지 못하는 장면까지 겹치면 밑줄 문장이 세운 '믿을 만한 번역자' 역할이 뒤집히는 반어로 읽히므로 B가 정답이다. A는 표면 기능만, C는 바로 뒤 문장과의 대조만 본 것이며, D는 지문과 양립하지만 번역의 차이라는 핵심 단서를 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: Promises are cheap on a tram line. That was my mother's saying, and I repeated it the winter I rode Moana's bus each morning to the weaving cooperative on Ponsonby Road. __Moana kept a child's drawing of a red kite pinned above the fare box, its corners curling from the heat of the engine.__ At the cooperative we were finishing a flax mat for a wedding, and I spent most days arguing with the other women about a border pattern none of us would agree to tighten. One morning Moana missed my stop and drove two streets past it before he noticed, apologizing so many times that I laughed at him. In late August his route changed, and a new driver took the bus. The drawing was gone from above the fare box. That Saturday, walking home, I saw Moana on the hill above the harbor, holding the string of a red kite while a small girl in a borrowed coat ran beneath it, shouting at the wind.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It adds a homely detail that describes the interior of the bus the narrator rides.
It introduces a lighthearted note that prepares for Moana's apology for the missed stop.
It introduces an object that points toward a pledge Moana eventually keeps for a child.
It supports the mother's saying by showing how small tokens fade over time.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 처음에는 버스 내부를 보여 주는 소박한 배경 묘사로 읽힌다. 그러나 노선이 바뀐 뒤 그림이 사라졌다는 문장과, 토요일에 Moana가 실제 빨간 연을 들고 아이와 함께 있는 결말 장면이 이어지면서 그 그림은 아이에게 한 약속의 표지였음이 드러난다. 첫 문장의 '약속은 값싸다'는 속담과도 반어적으로 맞물리므로 C가 정답이다. A는 표면 기능만, B는 다음 장면의 사과와 엮은 오독이며, D는 속담 표현을 빌려 일반화했지만 결말 장면과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: "We called your grandfather Arslan in those days," Kerem said, for the third time that week, and Emre stabbed at his rice. Kerem ran the camp dining hall as if it were a ship, banging a ladle on the counter at seven sharp and grumbling that boys today could not peel an onion. Emre told the other counselors the old man was a fossil in an apron. He was not lying, exactly; he was leaving things out. He did not mention that Kerem had driven four hours to the funeral in March and stood at the back the whole time. On the last night, while the hall emptied, Emre stayed behind to stack the benches. By the stove he found the cook's notebook of recipes and, under a dish marked only for the Lion, copied the list of spices onto a napkin. Then he wiped the counter where Kerem always leaned and hung the ladle back on its hook, handle out.
items.question: Which choice best describes Emre's attitude toward Kerem as conveyed in the text?
options: Deep respect for Kerem's loyalty to his family while he mocks him in front of others
Real admiration for Kerem's skill in the kitchen while he mocks him in front of others
Mild irritation at Kerem's strict routines while he tolerates him for the rest of the summer
Amused patience with Kerem as an old fossil while he endures the stories about Arslan
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Emre는 Kerem을 '앞치마 두른 화석'이라 부르며 놀리지만, 곧 '거짓말은 아니었다, 정확히는'이라는 자기 정정이 나온다. 이어 Kerem이 장례식에 네 시간을 운전해 왔다는 사실, 그리고 마지막 밤 Emre가 '사자를 위한' 요리법을 베껴 적고 조리대를 닦아 주는 행동이 드러난다. 말투 아래에는 할아버지에 대한 Kerem의 의리를 향한 깊은 존중이 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 존중의 이유를 요리 솜씨로 바꿨고, C는 말투만 읽은 해석이며, D는 '화석'이라는 지문 표현을 빌렸지만 행동 단서를 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: "Your tomatoes are leaning again," Hana called across the fence, and I pretended not to hear her. Twenty years ago we had shared a stage in Bologna, she the soprano everyone remembered and I the mezzo who sang the second verse. I liked to tell the garden committee that her famous high note had been mostly nerve and good lighting. That was not unfair, exactly, though it was not the whole of it. Last spring the conductor's widow, sorting his papers, sent me a letter he had written long ago: Hana had refused the solo in Vienna unless I was hired too. I read it on the bench beside the compost bins and then folded it into my seed catalog. Since then I have been the one who waters both our plots on Thursdays, when her knees are bad. I tie her tomatoes to the stakes with strips of an old scarf. When she thanks me, I tell her the vines were blocking my sun.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Hana?
options: Lingering envy of Hana's fame while she helps her out of plain neighborly habit
Quiet gratitude for Hana's past loyalty while she keeps up a show of complaint
Renewed admiration for Hana's singing talent while she tends her plot out of pity
Amused scorn for the high note's nerve while she works beside Hana in the garden
items.explanation: 화자는 앞부분에서 Hana의 유명한 고음이 '배짱과 조명' 덕분이었다고 깎아내리지만, '불공평한 말은 아니었다, 정확히는'이라며 스스로 말을 고친다. 지휘자의 편지로 Hana가 화자를 함께 고용하지 않으면 독창을 거절했다는 사실을 알게 된 뒤, 화자는 목요일마다 두 텃밭에 물을 주고 토마토를 묶어 준다. 불평하는 말투와 조용한 행동을 겹치면 과거의 의리에 대한 감사가 드러나므로 B가 정답이다. A는 말투만, C는 존중의 이유를 재능과 동정으로 바꾼 것이며, D는 지문 어휘를 빌렸지만 편지 이후의 행동을 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage:
I say the bread comes late again, Mio,
and the crust is soft as an excuse.
I say it to the counter, to the coffee,
to the road outside where the trucks don't stop.
Felix would have shouted. Felix kept
a ledger of every coin you took that spring
before you learned to knock instead of climb.
I am not keeping one, or not exactly;
I only know the number by heart.
Mornings, I leave the side door on the latch.
I set the second cup out on the counter,
the one with the chipped blue rim,
and pour it before your engine reaches the hill.
When you come in shaking rain from your collar,
I tell you the coffee is stale, drink it anyway,
and push the old ledger, unopened, under the till.
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward Mio?
options: Lasting resentment toward Mio for the theft while she puts up with his deliveries
Gentle kindness toward Mio out of guilt over Felix while she complains about the bread
Tacit acceptance of Mio as welcome while she keeps the old wrong in mind
Weary irritation at soft crusts while she tolerates the boy for the diner's sake
items.explanation: 시의 앞부분에서 화자는 빵이 늦고 껍질이 무르다고 투덜대며, Felix가 Mio가 훔친 동전을 장부에 적어 두었다고 말한다. 중간의 '장부를 쓰지 않는다, 정확히는'이라는 정정은 화자가 그 일을 잊지 않았음을 보여 준다. 그러나 후반에서 화자는 옆문을 열어 두고 Mio의 두 번째 잔을 미리 따르며 장부를 펼치지 않은 채 밀어 넣으므로, 잘못을 기억하면서도 그를 받아들이는 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 투덜대는 말투만 읽은 것이고, B는 친절의 이유를 Felix에 대한 죄책감으로 바꾼 선택지다.

items.passage: Years later, I still describe my mother-in-law as the most exhausting woman in Busan. Danish read in the library on Jungang Street every afternoon and corrected my Korean in a whisper loud enough for the librarians to hear. She found my handwriting careless and my soup thin, and she said so. I tell all this as a comedy at dinners now, and it is not a false story, exactly; it is a story with a page left out. In my first winter, a firm in Accra offered me a post and a ticket home, and I spent a week deciding. During that week Danish sat beside me each afternoon and taught me the characters for every street between the library and our flat, saying nothing about the letter. I turned the post down in March. When the library closed for repairs last year, I was the one who carried her reading lamp home, wrapped in my own coat, and set it on the shelf I can see from my desk.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Danish?
options: Lingering resentment of Danish's harsh criticism while she turns those memories into dinner jokes
Tender regard for Danish born of guilt over the job while she jokes about the past
Amused exasperation at Danish's corrections while she treats the old quarrels as comedy
Deep attachment to Danish for that week of help while she keeps the old complaints alive
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 시어머니를 부산에서 가장 피곤한 사람이라 부르며 그 시절을 코미디처럼 이야기한다. 그러나 '거짓 이야기는 아니다, 정확히는'이라는 정정 뒤에, 떠날 기회를 고민하던 한 주 동안 Danish가 말없이 길 이름 글자를 가르쳐 준 일이 드러난다. 끝에서 화자가 그녀의 독서등을 자기 코트로 감싸 집에 가져와 늘 보이는 곳에 둔 행동은 그 한 주에서 비롯된 깊은 애착을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A와 C는 불평과 농담의 말투만 읽었고, B는 애정의 이유를 화자 자신의 죄책감으로 뒤집었다.

items.passage: When my grandfather moved into our flat above the terraced gardens in Manila, he brought three suitcases and a Greek grammar for me. Stavros had decided I would learn his language by summer, and every evening on the terrace he drilled verbs while the neighbors' radios played. I complained to my friends that he taught like a drill sergeant with a cough. For my birthday he gave me a wool sweater, knitted by his sister in Thessaloniki, in a city where the evenings rarely drop below twenty-five degrees. I told him it was perfect. That was not a lie, exactly; it was a word I had just learned from him. I wore it to every lesson on the terrace, sweating, until the cuffs stretched past my wrists. Now I keep the grammar on my desk with his pencil marks in the margins, and I conjugate one verb aloud each morning before I open the window.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Stavros?
options: Devoted affection for Stavros and his efforts while she grumbles about his strict lessons
Mild annoyance at Stavros's nightly drilling while she endures the lessons out of duty
Respectful fondness for Stavros out of pity for his move while she resists his teaching
Amused tolerance of the drill sergeant's habits while she plays along with the sweater
items.explanation: 화자는 친구들에게 할아버지가 '기침하는 훈련 교관'처럼 가르친다고 불평하지만, 맞지 않는 털 스웨터를 '완벽하다'고 말한 것은 '거짓말은 아니었다, 정확히는'이라며 정정한다. 이후 화자는 땀을 흘리면서도 수업마다 그 스웨터를 입었고, 지금도 매일 아침 동사 하나를 소리 내어 활용한다. 투덜대는 말투와 지속적인 행동을 함께 보면 할아버지와 그의 노력에 대한 깊은 애정이 드러나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 말투만 읽은 것이고, C는 애정의 이유를 동정으로 바꿨으며, D는 지문 표현을 빌렸지만 현재의 행동을 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage: Chiang Mai had not wanted their music that season. Nguyen and Budi played the fiddle and the khim in a hotel courtyard to rows of empty chairs, and by October the manager was paying them in rice. To cover the rent they took work at a ceramics studio by the river, where Budi glazed bowls quickly and Nguyen, who had never touched clay, broke more than he carried. In November the khim's hammers went to a pawnshop, and Budi stopped speaking of the duo at all. Some nights Nguyen stayed at the studio after the others had left, and in the mornings the small kiln was still warm. In December the hotel asked them to play once more, for a wedding in the courtyard. Budi arrived with empty hands. Nguyen took from his coat two slender hammers, their heads capped with fired clay and glazed the pale green Budi used on his bowls. Budi turned them over slowly, then sat down at the khim.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The duo's lack of listeners forces the two musicians to seek other kinds of work.
A trade taken up out of need becomes the source of a gift that revives the pair.
A carefully made gift allows the two musicians to perform together at the wedding.
Budi's silence about the duo is what drives Nguyen to stay late in the studio.
items.explanation: 앞부분의 사건은 청중이 없어 두 연주자가 생계를 위해 도자기 공방에 일하러 가는 장면으로, 음악의 쇠퇴처럼 보인다. 중간에는 Nguyen이 밤늦게 공방에 남고 가마가 아침까지 따뜻하다는 설명 없는 디테일이 놓인다. 뒷부분에서 Nguyen이 Budi의 유약 색으로 구운 점토 채를 내놓으면서, 생계 때문에 시작한 일이 듀오를 되살리는 선물의 원천이 되었음이 드러나므로 B가 정답이다. A는 첫 사건만, C는 둘째 사건만 요약했고, D는 인과의 방향을 지문과 다르게 세운 선택지다.

items.passage: By the spring I turned fifteen, I had cooked every meal in my aunt's flat above the radio repair shop in Seville for two years. Remedios mended wirelesses downstairs and spoke to me mostly in instructions: less salt, more oil, close the door against the solder smoke. That April a neighbor borrowed our good copper pan for a christening and did not bring it back. I fried eggs in a dented tin pot and complained about it at every meal, while my aunt only turned the dial of whatever set lay open on her bench. In May she began working late, and a smell of hot metal drifted up the stairs past midnight. On my saint's day I found a new pan on the stove, hammered from the brass casing of an old radio cabinet, its handle wrapped in copper wire from the shop. Remedios was already downstairs, bent over a set, her back to the stairs.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A neighbor's thoughtless borrowing leaves a young cook with poor tools for her work.
A handmade pan arrives to replace the copper one on the narrator's saint's day.
An aunt's seeming indifference turns out to conceal a reply made with her own craft.
The aunt's new pan is what finally ends the narrator's habit of complaining at meals.
items.explanation: 첫 사건에서 화자는 이웃이 가져간 구리 냄비 때문에 끼니마다 불평하지만, 고모 Remedios는 라디오 다이얼만 돌리며 무심해 보인다. 중간에는 고모가 밤늦게 일하고 뜨거운 금속 냄새가 올라온다는 설명 없는 디테일이 놓인다. 뒷사건에서 라디오 케이스의 황동과 가게의 구리선으로 만든 냄비가 나타나면서, 무관심처럼 보였던 태도가 사실은 자기 기술로 한 대답이었음이 드러나므로 C가 정답이다. A는 첫 사건만, B는 둘째 사건만 요약했고, D는 냄비와 불평의 관계를 지문에 없는 결과로 세운 선택지다.

items.passage: We ran a tailoring shop on a street in Tehran that had too many tailors, and by the third winter the ledger was mostly red. My brother Kemoy cut the cloth; I, Hemi, did the seams, the buttonholes, the slow finishing. When a colonel's wife praised a coat in the window, Kemoy accepted her compliments at the counter while I sat in the back with pins in my mouth. I said nothing then, and I said a good deal later, on the roof, where we hung the shop's linen to dry. For a month after that we pinned our cloths at opposite ends of the line. In March the colonel's wife returned for a second coat and asked for the tailor who had finished the first. Kemoy did not answer her. He walked to the back of the shop, took my hand, which was still holding a needle, and led me out to the counter. That evening on the roof he hung his cloths next to mine.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A failing shop strains two brothers who share the work of making each coat.
A customer's return allows the narrator to receive praise for his careful finishing.
The brothers' quarrel on the roof is what drives the colonel's wife to return.
An earlier slight over recognition is repaired through an act instead of an apology.
items.explanation: 첫 사건에서 형 Kemoy는 손님의 칭찬을 혼자 받고, 마무리 작업을 한 화자는 뒤편에 앉아 있다가 나중에 옥상에서 따진다. 중간에는 한 달 동안 빨랫줄 양 끝에 따로 빨래를 너는 미해결 장면이 놓인다. 뒷사건에서 Kemoy는 아무 말 없이 화자의 손을 잡고 계산대로 데려가므로, 공로를 둘러싼 서운함이 사과의 말 대신 행동으로 회복되었다는 D가 정답이다. A는 첫 사건만, B는 둘째 사건만 요약했고, C는 다툼과 손님 재방문 사이의 인과를 지문에 없게 세운 선택지다.

items.passage: Dry leaves filled the stone basin of the fountain in our courtyard in Taipei, and every autumn Baoyu came to argue with me about them. He was my father's oldest friend, and he arrived each October with a rake, insisting that the leaves be burned, while I insisted they be left for mulch. My father had sailed for Fujian when I was nine and had sent two letters since. Baoyu never spoke of him. We argued about leaves for six autumns, loudly enough that the neighbors leaned out of their windows. One year he brought a small tin box along with the rake and set it on the fountain's rim; I did not open it, and he did not mention it. The seventh October he did not come. A boy brought the rake and the tin box to the gate with a note in Baoyu's hand: the leaves are yours to decide now. Inside the box were my father's letters to him, thirty of them, every one asking about me.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A minor yearly dispute proves to have stood in for a larger matter left unsaid.
An old family friend keeps up a garden custom after the narrator's father departs.
A box of letters shows that the narrator's father wrote more often than she knew.
The narrator's refusal to burn the leaves is what leads Baoyu to stop visiting.
items.explanation: 첫 사건은 아버지의 오랜 친구 Baoyu와 화자가 해마다 낙엽을 태울지 말지를 두고 다투는 장면이며, Baoyu는 아버지에 대해 한 번도 말하지 않는다. 중간에는 Baoyu가 가져왔지만 아무도 열지 않은 양철 상자라는 미해결 디테일이 놓인다. 마지막에 그 상자 속에서 화자의 안부를 묻는 아버지의 편지 서른 통이 나오면서, 작은 낙엽 다툼이 말하지 못한 더 큰 문제를 대신해 왔음이 드러나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 첫 사건만, C는 둘째 사건만 요약했고, D는 방문이 끊긴 원인을 지문 근거 없이 화자의 거절로 세웠다.

items.passage: Four things Ama demanded of an apprentice: sharp chisels, swept floors, silence while she measured, and one finished piece before the passes opened. That winter the snow shut us into the cabin above the valley outside Lima for nine days. Each morning Ama took a small photograph from her coat, glanced at it, and slid it face down beneath the glue pot. On the third day she told me to build a frame of cedar, five inches by seven. "Good practice for mitered corners," she said. I cut the corners badly twice, and she made me do them again. On the ninth day, the date written in pencil on the back of the cedar plank she had chosen for me, she declared the frame finished, though I could still see a gap at one joint. She set the photograph into it without letting me look. Later, sweeping, I turned it over: a young man with my chin, holding a plane, and Ama beside him, both of them covered in shavings.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Ama most likely have the narrator build the frame?
options: She wants the narrator to practice mitered corners before the mountain passes open.
She wants the narrator's own work to honor a person tied to both of them.
She wants to keep the narrator busy during the long days the snow traps them.
She wants to make up for her harsh demands by giving the narrator a keepsake.
items.explanation: Ama가 직접 댄 이유는 '연귀 맞춤 연습'이지만, 그녀는 매일 아침 사진을 꺼내 보고 엎어 두는 습관을 보인다. 또 그녀가 골라 준 판자 뒤에는 날짜가 적혀 있고, 바로 그날 이음매에 틈이 남았는데도 액자를 완성으로 선언한다. 끝에서 사진 속 인물이 화자와 턱이 닮은 젊은 목수와 Ama임이 드러나므로, 두 사람 모두와 이어진 인물을 화자의 손으로 기리려 했다는 B가 정답이다. A는 표면 명분만 받아들여 날짜에 맞춘 완성을 설명하지 못하고, C와 D는 같은 행동을 다른 감정으로 설명하지만 날짜와 사진 단서와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Years later I can still hear the tin cup clinking against the water jars. During the week I spent at the ranger station after losing the trail, Rashid and I filled the jars from the cistern each evening, he pouring and I counting aloud, until the counting became a kind of evening prayer neither of us named. When my ankle healed, I said I would take the night bus down to Marrakesh. Rashid said he had business at the post office in the city and would ride along. I learned later that he had bought both tickets two days before I mentioned leaving, and had folded his into the back of his permit book. On the bus he hardly slept. At the halfway stop, in the dark, he climbed down, filled the tin cup at the station tap, and passed it up to me through the window. Then he took his seat again, and at Marrakesh he walked with me as far as my hotel before turning back toward the station.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Rashid most likely ride the night bus with the narrator?
options: He needs to handle some business at the post office in the city.
He wants to make sure the narrator's healed ankle holds up on the journey.
He wants to carry on a shared evening custom until their time together ends.
He feels responsible for the narrator having lost the trail near his station.
items.explanation: Rashid가 밝힌 이유는 우체국 볼일이지만, 앞부분에서 두 사람은 매일 저녁 물 항아리를 채우며 숫자를 세는 일을 기도처럼 반복한다. 중간에는 그가 화자가 떠나겠다고 말하기 이틀 전에 이미 표 두 장을 사 두었다는 시점 단서가 있다. 끝에서 그는 한밤 정류장에서 양철 컵에 물을 채워 건네므로, 함께한 저녁 의식을 헤어질 때까지 이어 가려 했다는 C가 정답이다. A는 표면 명분만 믿어 미리 산 표를 설명하지 못하고, B와 D는 같은 동행을 다른 걱정이나 책임감으로 설명하지만 컵과 물이라는 끝 동작과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Brine and coal smoke: that was the smell of the crossing on the salt flats east of Manchester, where my father ran the little ferry over the brine channel for thirty years. Every April a passenger named Josiah bought two tickets and rode alone, standing at the stern with his hat in his hands, and he left the second ticket tucked into the rail. My father punched both without a word and never asked whose the second one was. The year after my father died, Josiah came on the usual morning and said, "Good day, Miss Mabel," as if nothing had changed. I told him the ferry was closed for repairs to the engine, which was true. I had booked those repairs myself, for that exact week, in January. That afternoon I rowed him across in my father's old skiff, the slow way, with the oars creaking in their locks, and on the far bank I took two tickets from my coat and punched them both.
items.question: Based on the text, why does the narrator most likely arrange the engine repairs for that week?
options: She needs the engine mended before the busier months on the channel arrive.
She wants to avoid charging Josiah a fare in the year her father died.
She hopes the delay will lead Josiah to explain the second ticket at last.
She wants to carry Josiah across herself in the way her father would.
items.explanation: 화자가 댄 표면 이유는 엔진 수리이고, 그 말 자체는 사실로 제시된다. 그러나 앞부분에서 아버지는 해마다 Josiah의 표 두 장을 말없이 찍어 주었고, 중간에서 화자는 수리를 1월에 바로 '그 주'로 직접 잡아 두었다고 밝힌다. 끝에서 화자는 아버지의 낡은 작은 배로 Josiah를 직접 건네주고 표 두 장을 찍으므로, 아버지가 하던 방식대로 그를 몸소 건네주려 했다는 D가 정답이다. A는 표면 명분만 받아들여 수리 시점을 설명하지 못하고, B와 C는 다른 동기로 행동을 설명하지만 표를 찍는 마지막 동작과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Who prints a town's wedding programs for free for nineteen years? I do, apparently. The press room behind the hardware store in Albuquerque smells of ink and machine oil, and the old press clanks like a washing machine full of forks. Camille has packed his boxes by the door: books, a lamp, the radio he never fixed. People stop me at the grocery to say they still have the program from their daughter's wedding. They mean it kindly. I tell them the cardstock was on sale. This morning Camille set the type for one last job, a church supper flyer, and misspelled casserole. I left it. While he loaded the car, I locked a fresh frame into the press, inked the plate, and ran a single sheet with his name centered in the large wooden letters I save for brides. I folded it twice, slid it into the side pocket of his duffel bag, and went back to cleaning the rollers.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Wry and tender toward her son as he leaves home
Cheerful and relieved toward her son as he leaves home
Dry and amused toward the town that praises her free work
Wistful and tender toward the years of her printing work
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 19년간 무료로 인쇄해 왔다는 사실을 '그런가 보다'라고 비꼬고, 칭찬에는 카드지가 세일이었다고 건조하게 답한다. 중간에 아들이 틀린 철자를 그냥 두는 멈칫하는 디테일이 놓인다. 끝에서 화자는 신부에게만 쓰던 큰 나무 활자로 아들의 이름을 찍어 가방에 몰래 넣으므로, 겉의 건조한 유머 아래 떠나는 아들을 향한 다정함이 있는 A가 정답이다. C는 겉 어조만 잡았고, B는 속 어조의 원인을 안도로 뒤집었으며, D는 같은 감정을 인쇄 일 전체로 넓혀 마지막 동작의 대상과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: "Mind the corner; it has gone slack," Ingeborg said, before she had even removed her gloves. We had not spoken in eleven years. The banner lay where I had unrolled it across the floor of the school gymnasium, between the vaulting horse and the ropes, its border of Rotterdam's bridges half stitched. Our mother had begun it for the school's jubilee; we had quarrelled over the colour of the river and left it in a trunk. I offered Ingeborg the stool, as one offers a visitor. She took the floor instead, kneeling where she had always knelt, on the left. We worked until the lamps were lit, speaking only of thread prices and the caretaker's cough. Once she reached for the grey silk, paused, and took the blue. I said nothing. When the caretaker came to lock the doors, she rolled up her half of the banner with mine inside it, the way our mother used to, so that neither end would crease.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Formal and distant toward a sister who has returned as a visitor
Restrained and hopeful toward the sisters' slow return to each other
Restrained and anxious toward a quarrel that may soon begin again
Nostalgic and hopeful toward their mother's memory and her craft
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 두 자매는 11년 만에 만나 방문객을 대하듯 의자를 권하고 실값과 관리인의 기침 같은 이야기만 나눠 겉으로는 격식 있고 절제된 어조를 보인다. 중간에 언니가 회색 실을 집으려다 멈추고 파란 실을 택하는 장면은 예전 다툼의 원인이었던 강 색깔에서 한발 물러서는 몸짓이다. 끝에서 언니가 어머니처럼 두 반쪽을 함께 말아 구김이 가지 않게 하므로, 절제 아래 화해의 희망이 깔린 B가 정답이다. A는 겉 층만 읽었고, C는 속 층의 원인을 불안으로 뒤집었으며, D는 같은 감정을 어머니의 기억으로 옮겨 대상이 어긋난다.

items.passage: When I was sixteen, my violin lessons took place in the back room of a seed-saving cooperative in Tromso, between shelves of labeled envelopes: dwarf peas, northern kale, a barley nobody had planted since 1950. Anders, my teacher, sorted seeds while I played and corrected my bowing without looking up. In March he informed me that he had entered me in the conservatory audition in Oslo, with a sonata he had picked out himself. He had not asked. I said thank you in the tone one uses for a parking ticket. For three months I practiced the sonata in that room, and he sorted seeds, and neither of us mentioned the entry form. The night before I left, I found a paper envelope in my violin case, labeled in his square handwriting: barley, 1950, keep dry. I have it still. I have not planted it, and I have not thrown it away.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Irritated and cold toward a teacher who overstepped in the narrator's affairs
Wry and relieved toward a choice the teacher made for the narrator
Wry and grateful toward a teacher who acted on the narrator's behalf
Wry and grateful toward the old seeds stored in the cooperative
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 묻지도 않고 오디션에 등록한 선생님에게 '주차 딱지 받을 때의 말투'로 고맙다고 했다며 건조하게 비꼰다. 중간에는 석 달 동안 두 사람 모두 신청서 이야기를 꺼내지 않는 어긋난 침묵이 놓인다. 끝에서 화자는 선생님이 넣어 준 1950년 보리 씨앗 봉투를 심지도 버리지도 않고 간직하므로, 겉의 비꼼 아래 자신을 위해 결정해 준 선생님에 대한 감사가 깔린 C가 정답이다. A는 겉 층만 읽었고, B는 속 층의 원인을 부담에서 벗어난 안도로 뒤집었으며, D는 감사의 대상을 씨앗으로 옮겨 범위가 어긋난다.

items.passage: Chalk dust covered my sleeves by the time the evening class ended at the language school on Hang Bai Street. Lan stayed behind, as she had every Tuesday since she moved back to Hanoi, and addressed me as Teacher Anh, the way the other students did. I called her Miss Lan and corrected her English verbs. My younger brother, who was nine, still asked why she had stopped coming to our house after her family left for Da Nang. I had told him she was busy. That Tuesday Lan handed me an envelope: the tuition I had waived for her in September, counted out in small notes. I pushed it back across the desk. She left it on my brother's school notebook, which I had been marking during the break. Before she went, she copied a sentence into its margin in careful English, I am sorry I did not say goodbye, and drew a small bicycle beside it, the kind we used to ride along the lake.
items.question: Which choice best describes the relationship between the narrator and Lan?
options: A teacher and an adult student whose dealings stay within the classroom's polite rules
A teacher who has generously helped a struggling student by waiving her class fees
Former friends in which the narrator works to win back a friend who drifted off
Former friends behind formal titles, in which Lan takes on the work of making amends
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 두 사람은 '선생님 Anh', 'Miss Lan'이라는 공식 호칭을 쓰며 교실 예절 안에 머무는 것처럼 보인다. 중간에서 Lan은 화자가 면제해 준 수업료를 작은 지폐로 되돌려 주고, 화자가 밀어내도 남동생의 공책 위에 두고 간다. 끝에서 Lan이 동생에게 작별 인사를 못 한 것을 사과하는 문장과 함께 예전에 둘이 타던 자전거를 그려 넣으므로, 격식 뒤의 옛 친구 관계에서 Lan이 먼저 관계를 회복하려 한다는 D가 정답이다. A는 호칭만 본 공식 관계이고, B는 수업료 장면 하나만 반영했으며, C는 관계를 되돌리려는 쪽의 방향을 화자로 뒤집었다.
